approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It keeps a small population of high-scoring parents, while an archive of all accepted observations trains a fingerprint Gaussian process. Correlated draws from that model select which fresh offspring receive evaluations. The Parent also checks that each pool molecule has a stable canonical identity, so uniqueness and later feedback use consistent keys. Its edits readily change individual atoms, but offer no direct way to reverse an intact amide between two attached fragments.
approach.novelty: Add a direct orientation reversal of an acyclic secondary amide. Keep both attached fragments and the complete amide group, and exchange which fragment connects through nitrogen and which through the carbonyl carbon. The move becomes available when the existing atom-replacement draw lands on an eligible carbonyl carbon whose ordinary replacement menu is empty. Earlier siblings protected carbonyl endpoints, retained ring cores, or relocated nitrogen within an aromatic ring. This experiment changes the direction of a complete amide relationship, giving the existing learned selector a new local alternative without growing or trimming the molecule.

hypothesis: Enable a direct formula-preserving reversal of an acyclic secondary amide at an otherwise empty carbonyl-carbon replacement site, exchanging the nitrogen-side and carbonyl-side attachment relationships while retaining both external fragments.

finding_summary.headline: Eight evaluated amide-reversal descendants retained the edit, but mean score fell by 0.02036
finding_summary.insights: Failure to generate, preserve or evaluate a reversed amide is ruled out as the explanation for the missed score target. The direct comparisons show limited measured benefit: three source pairs tie, including the leading sampled amide pair, and the only incumbent gain combines two edits. The largest task-level loss occurred in docking, where 20 reversal-bearing candidates entered pools but none was selected. That loss cannot be read as an observed penalty on a scored reversed amide; opening an empty-menu action changes later random draws, pool composition and search history even when the new alternative is unselected. A contribution probe that distinguishes the local alternative's value from these trajectory changes remains informative. The change also does not establish globally better chemistry. Eligible-amide-containing emissions increased from 328 to 563, yet measured nonaromatic C(=O)-N coverage stayed nearly flat at 1,669 versus 1,667 molecules, and mean heavy-atom count increased from 33.39 to 35.43. The molecular assessment associates the weak docking seed with a less aliphatic-amine-rich branch and still finds reactive linkages, oversized repeated cores and unspecified stereochemistry. These are descriptive associations, not causal functional-group effects. The evidence supports a narrowly correct local transformation with sparse direct score exposure; broader utility and practical chemical quality remain open.
finding_summary.results: Every one of the 120 selected eligible sites produced a checked, identity-changing reversal while preserving formula, size, the complete local amide and both attached fragments. Of 95 pooled descendants, 93 retained the reversed orientation; all eight descendants selected for evaluation retained it. Two later edits destroyed the amide, and a double reversal returned to an already seen molecule and was rejected as a duplicate. Of four evaluated sole reversals of accepted parents, one improved its source score by 0.011119 and three tied; none created a new incumbent. A reversal followed by deletion produced one incumbent gain, improving its real parent's score by 0.049026, but that gain cannot be assigned to the reversal alone. All 15 task/seed sessions completed their budgets with no invalid or duplicate oracle submissions. Mean final-best score fell from 0.544374 to 0.524013, a decline of 0.020361 instead of the registered minimum gain of 0.002. Population standard deviation across seed means fell from 0.013310 to 0.007408. Every seed's macro score declined; the 15 paired task outcomes comprised three wins, eight losses and four ties. The inherited identity checker also rejected two unstable candidates before pooling, while every admitted identity remained stable.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles retain useful amides and amines, but reactive bonds, oversized repeats and unspecified stereochemistry persist.
molecular.overall_character: Read the complete Child and Parent panels for seeds 0, 1 and 2 on every supplied task. Each Child task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The output is dominated by substituted aromatic and heteroaromatic ring systems, with secondary amides, cyclic carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles, ethers, amines and halogens. Saturated and bridged nitrogen rings are well represented in some streams; ring chemistry is not missing. Digest ring-closure presence rates range from 0.9747 to 0.9931, and aromatic-atom presence rates from 0.9414 to 0.9885. These are SMILES-text presence rates, not ring counts or fractions of atoms that are aromatic. There is moderate structural variety across seeds, but each seed repeatedly revisits its own ring family. Plausibility is mixed: conventional secondary amides and aminomethyl heterocycles coexist with N-halogen bonds, O-halogen bonds, peroxides, unusual ring fusions and very large repeated heterocycles. All task digests have stereocentre_rate 0.0: no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry is recorded, although several saturated ring structures contain potential stereocentres. Almost entirely uncharged strings do not establish absence of protonatable amines. Size and functional-group descriptions below are structural readings of the supplied SMILES; reported objective values are existing trajectory values. The chemical observations do not establish synthesis routes, binding poses or activation of the registered mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly moderate-sized substituted fused heterocycles: mean SMILES length 46.5, with ring and aromatic presence both 0.9839 and halogen presence 0.9713. The leading seed-1 molecules are indoles connected by a secondary carboxamide to fluoropyridine, carrying methoxy, ethyl, vinyl and additional aryl halogen substituents. The leading cited molecule contains 26 heavy atoms. Both amide orientations occur. Seed 0 instead develops more extensively fused, N-methylated rings with imine or oxime linkers; seed 2 includes rearranged sulfur-containing fused rings and N-N-containing acyl linkers. These alternatives are much less conventional than the straightforward indole amides. The end of seed 2 still includes a peroxide-bearing, N-fluorinated amidine analogue and a small carbamoyl fluoride fragment.
liabilities: Near-leading molecules contain N-Br or N-F bonds, including a benzene-fused four-membered nitrogen ring. Chemical parseability does not establish its stability or synthetic accessibility.
Other cited proposals contain peroxide, hydrazine-like N-N or imine functionality, and terminal proposals can collapse to small reactive fragments instead of preserving the ring system.
missing_features: Retention of a complete heteroaromatic partner and intact secondary amide is inconsistent across proposals, although the leading seed shows both and the fragmented tail lacks them.

Chemically conservative variation around the leading ring/amide relationship is limited compared with ring contraction and N-halogenation. An absent target-specific scaffold or a required amide direction cannot be inferred from these scores.

Seed-1 evaluations 164 and 189 retain the same substituted fragments but reverse the secondary-amide orientation; both score 0.41605207864642335. The chlorine alternatives also tie at that value. Evaluations 250 and 269 are another opposite-orientation pair tied at 0.41003927643747895. Thus the observed series supports retaining the substantial heteroaromatic/amide architecture and changing substituents, but demonstrates no score preference between these sampled amide orientations. The contracted-ring compound with N-Br and N-F at evaluation 288 still scores 0.4136551925282466, so the score does not cleanly separate chemically conventional amides from reactive alternatives. Tiny F, FF and carbon fragments score 0.0; the final carbamoyl fluoride scores 3.5259015803172243e-12. Relative to Parent, seed 0 moves from a fused heterocyclic ketone at 0.4463521672202675 to an oxime-bearing best at 0.3779802455230667; seed 1 reaches the intact-amide series at 0.41605207864642335 versus Parent 0.4126819838532174. per_task.generated_character: This is the largest output stream: mean SMILES length 102.5 and maximum 235; ring and aromatic presence are both 0.9885. Seed 0 produces fused aza-aromatic and pyrone-like carbonyl/ether rings connected through aminomethyl or amidine groups, often with long unsaturated ether tails. Its best cited molecule has 39 heavy atoms. Seed 1 combines aza-aromatic carbonyl/oxygen rings, multiple aryl/alkenyl halogens, an ethynyl group and an O-C#N cyanate linkage; its best has 46 heavy atoms. Seed 2 repeatedly joins fused nitrogen heterocycles containing cyclic carbonyl groups into very large assemblies; the final cited molecule has 59 heavy atoms. Conventional heteroaromatic substructures are recognizable, but the complete substituted polyenes and repeated assemblies have questionable practical accessibility.
liabilities: Long polyene and imine/oxime-ether tails have unspecified geometric isomerism and chemically sensitive unsaturation; several high-scoring analogues add N-F or multiply halogenated carbon centres.

The seed-1 cyanate linkage and the large, densely fused or repeated nitrogen/carbonyl assemblies require chemical scrutiny. Ring richness and a nonzero score do not supply a plausible route to these complete molecules.
missing_features: Compact arrangements that retain the productive heteroaromatic/carbonyl combination without repeated cores are not reliably maintained: a compact amidine example already scores close to the extended best, while the final seed-2 structures remain much larger.

The long unsaturated high-scoring series lacks defined alkene geometry and a consistent set of conventional, stable linkers. The trajectory does not establish that filling this practical chemistry gap would raise the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic carbonyl-rich molecule scores 0.548381482770623, while small CF, N#CCl and C#C fragments sit at 0.5. The seed-0 polyene ether reaches 0.6330703012912482, and the much smaller amidine-connected ring pair at evaluation 269 reaches 0.625077399380805. Consequently, the visible gradient rewards retained combinations of heteroaromatic/carbonyl environments but does not establish that a long tail or simple growth is necessary. The seed-1 halogenated cyanate reaches 0.6260015065397522; the huge final seed-2 assembly scores 0.6019296607531901. The Parent also generated elaborate carbonyl/aza-ring chemistry, including reactive O-halogen or N-halogen decorations. Parent/Child best values are 0.6004556752278376/0.6330703012912482 in seed 0, 0.6324703199409752/0.6260015065397522 in seed 1, and 0.6083454583246726/0.6049270072992701 in seed 2. The chemistry changes differently in each seed; persistent size and reactive-group liabilities are visible on both sides.

per_task.generated_character: Aromatic hydrophobic groups are combined with substantial saturated ring chemistry, rather than purely flat aromatic scaffolds. Mean SMILES length is 67.4; ring presence is 0.9897, aromatic presence 0.9816 and halogen presence 0.9908. Seed 0 develops fluoromethoxyphenyl groups, cyclobutanes, secondary/tertiary amines and bridged nitrogen rings with phenols and chlorine. Seed 2 develops medium-sized fused/spiro nitrogen rings linked through methylene to aryl sulfones or sulfoxides; its best contains 30 heavy atoms. Seed 1 instead favors brominated carbocycles, aryl sulfides/thiols and an aniline, with little of the unconjugated aliphatic amine character seen in the strongest other seeds. These are recognizable medicinal-chemistry ingredients, but strained polycycles, crowded halogenated aminals and unspecified configurations make many complete molecules questionable.
liabilities: Several high-scoring structures combine three- or four-membered nitrogen/carbon rings, congested bridgeheads and halogen-bearing aminal carbons. They require conformational and stability assessment beyond their accepted SMILES.
Dense halogen substitution, exposed phenols/thiols and variable sulfoxide configurations complicate chemical development. The low-score tail also includes reactive sulfonyl or sulfinyl halides.
missing_features: The seed-1 branch does not consistently combine aromatic hydrophobes with accessible nonacylated aliphatic amines, a combination present in the stronger Child seeds and in Parent best molecules. Aromatic aniline nitrogen or sulfonamide nitrogen is chemically different from that amine environment.

Explicit stereochemical specification is absent even in the bridged/spiro and substituted small-ring series. Their intended three-dimensional arrangement is unresolved by the supplied strings, and no score advantage from choosing a configuration has been measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading seed-2 cyclic-amine/aryl-sulfone molecule scores 0.9706475574822273, and the seed-0 polyamine with phenol/methoxy aromatics scores 0.9696022091086564. A carboxylic-acid/amide/sulfonamide molecule scores 0.0005876222816323224, while aryl sulfonyl bromide alone scores 0.0004426865581623269. The existing pattern associates substantial aromatic groups combined with nonacylated aliphatic amines and constrained ring shape with higher scores; amines alone are insufficient, since the initial piperidine-containing hydroxamate scores only 0.0003786988088202195. The seed-2 final aryl-depleted sulfur-containing analogue scores 0.3075949875612589, and seed 1 reaches only 0.7565380379187507 in its sulfide/thiol series. Parent best molecules carry aliphatic amines with aromatic groups in all seeds, at 0.9908331648929692, 0.9512348232667347 and 0.9914038363125457 respectively. The Child preserves that broad chemistry in seeds 0 and 2 but follows a less amine-rich branch in seed 1. These associations do not identify a receptor contact or isolate a causal functional-group effect.

per_task.generated_character: Moderate-sized, nitrogen- and carbonyl-rich polycycles dominate: mean SMILES length 56.8, ring presence 0.9931 and aromatic presence 0.9874. Seed 0 favors an alkylquinoline attached to a partially saturated bicyclic ring system with N-methyl lactam groups; the best cited molecule has 28 heavy atoms. Seed 1 combines phenyl and oxygen-containing fused aromatic rings with nitrogen-rich cyclic dicarbonyl scaffolds, including N-F substitution. Seed 2 uses alkylquinoline connected through N-O to a cyclic dicarbonyl amine system, sometimes extending that linkage to O-O-N. These streams explore saturated as well as aromatic rings but converge on related N-alkylated carbonyl ring families. The seed-0 leader is comparatively conventional; the N-halogen, N-N and peroxide-containing relatives weaken overall synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: N-F bonds, peroxide-containing O-O-N linkages and multiple N-N bonds occur among high-scoring examples, making score-based apparent quality a poor stand-in for stable, makeable chemistry.
Complex fused or bridged carbonyl-rich rings have unspecified stereochemistry, and terminal expansion can add redundant aromatic material without a corresponding higher recorded score.
missing_features: Stable alternatives retaining the observed aromatic-to-carbonyl/amine relationship are incompletely explored relative to N-F, N-N and O-O-N variants. The seed-0 best already shows that such reactive linkages are not necessary to reach this local score band.

Changes in ring topology and linker arrangement without simply appending another aromatic core remain limited within each converged family. The observed Parent and Child structures support alternative arrangements, but not a specific unseen target scaffold.

Seed-0 evaluation 281 combines quinoline with the partly saturated dicarbonyl/amine ring system at 0.21573006005788564; the N-demethylated analogue scores 0.21398574994084232. The N-F seed-1 leader scores 0.2133697489012744, and the N-O-linked seed-2 leader 0.2128343398267808. Its O-O-N relative remains at 0.2082817336272775. per_task.generated_character: The seeds separate into distinct chemical families. Seed 1 produces a compact fused nitrogen heterocycle with cyclic carbonyl groups, attached to fluorinated phenyl carrying aminomethyl or aminoethyl substituents; its best has 27 heavy atoms. transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied high-score excerpt contains intact secondary amides in both orientations with exact score ties, alongside a near-tied N-brominated/N-fluorinated contracted-ring analogue. Other streams retain high scores after introducing N-F or O-O-N linkages. An orientation alternative is already present; it does not eliminate the surrounding chemistry liabilities.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically conventional functional-group relationships are produced, but they are not reliably retained across further changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose ways to vary attached fragments and donor/acceptor placement while retaining complete conventional functional groups. Track the complete resulting group and its neighboring bonds through later edits, and let observed feedback determine usefulness; merely preserving a carbonyl or increasing amide-orientation coverage does not resolve this gap.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One stream contains a compact amidine-linked ring pair at 0.625077399380805 and a longer polyene analogue at 0.6330703012912482, while large repeated cyclic-carbonyl assemblies remain common. Elsewhere repeated ring assemblies score near zero, and small F, FF, carbon or halogen fragments appear at the bottom. Both excessive assembly and loss of essential molecular context are observed.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular size changes do not reliably preserve compact, chemically meaningful combinations of rings and substituents.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide controlled contraction and scaffold exchange that retain complete local functional-group and attachment relationships. Express comparable compact and expanded alternatives using generic molecular structure, without assuming that universally smaller or universally larger candidates are better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Some of the strongest recorded cyclic/aromatic molecules carry secondary or tertiary aliphatic amines, and another leading family carries aminomethyl or aminoethyl groups. Parallel seeds instead settle on amide/sulfonamide, aniline, sulfide/thiol or imine-rich chemistry. The generator can produce useful amine environments, but does not consistently offer them in alternative ring families.
transferable_gaps.gap: Accessible aliphatic amines and other conventional polar groups are unevenly represented across converged scaffold families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make comparable local alternatives available for neutral nonacylated amines, amides and other conventional polar groups while preserving the surrounding ring attachments. Distinguish their bonding environments structurally rather than treating all nitrogen substitutions as interchangeable; the objective feedback should determine which chemistry is useful.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied task digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0. Cited saturated bridgeheads, spiro or substituted small-ring structures contain unresolved potential stereocentres, and cited polyene tails do not specify alkene geometry. This is missing representation and sampling coverage, not demonstrated missing oracle utility.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemical and geometric alternatives are missing from molecules whose ring construction creates such distinctions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve chemically feasible stereochemistry when modifying saturated rings or unsaturated linkers, and expose explicit alternatives where the graph permits them. Assess those alternatives through ordinary feedback rather than assuming a particular configuration is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-closure presence is 0.9747 to 0.9931 across the supplied proposal sets, yet seeds repeatedly elaborate an indole/amide, cyclic-dicarbonyl aza-ring or halogenated polyamine family. Some alternatives add unusual fusions or repeat a core instead of changing its attachment geometry economically.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring abundance does not translate into broad coverage of plausible scaffold arrangements within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer local ring-topology or attachment changes that retain useful substituent and functional-group relationships, including alternatives of similar size. Track actual scaffold and attachment diversity independently of SMILES uniqueness, and use observed scores to decide where those alternatives matter.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

activation_observables.measurement: For every replace_atom invocation, reconstruct the selected atom and inherited element menu, then the exact eligibility rule on the recorded source. Count empty native menus with and without an eligible amide; attempted reversals; chemically checked successes; canonical identity changes versus symmetry identities; inner failures; temporary/global duplicates; novel pooled descendants; and actual evaluated descendants. The Parent has no direct reversal action. On an eligible selected site the Child must attempt the sole reversal without an additional random draw. applicability_conditions: This action applies only to the registered neutral acyclic secondary carboxamide with carbon substituents at both ends and the stated exclusion of an additional N/O/S double bond at the nitrogen-side external carbon. Lactams, tertiary/primary amides, ureas, carbamates, imides, isotopic local atoms and other ineligible functional groups retain their Parent behavior.

The formal Parent contains eligible initial and accepted molecules, but the inherited uniform site draw, accepted parent distribution and learned selection determine actual exposure. No site quota, special score treatment or task-specific routing is added, and a source opportunity is not evidence of a sampled or evaluated reversal.

The intervention preserves one complete amide and both external attachments during its immediate action. It does not globally protect carbonyls or prevent later native operators from changing the group. Symmetric substituent arrangements can yield the same canonical molecule, and return moves can collide with already emitted identities.

The former carbonyl carbon has an empty native substitution menu. Successful reversal therefore replaces an inner retry at that site and changes later RNG consumption and search history through the existing loop. Identical native choices on common inputs do not imply identical full trajectories or an unaffected control stream.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. approach.novelty: Add a direct orientation reversal of an acyclic secondary amide. Keep both attached fragments and the complete amide group, and exchange which fragment connects through nitrogen and which through the carbonyl carbon. The move becomes available when the existing atom-replacement draw lands on an eligible carbonyl carbon whose ordinary replacement menu is empty. Earlier siblings protected carbonyl endpoints, retained ring cores, or relocated nitrogen within an aromatic ring. This experiment changes the direction of a complete amide relationship, giving the existing learned selector a new local alternative without growing or trimming the molecule.

finding_summary.headline: Eight evaluated amide-reversal descendants retained the edit, but mean score fell by 0.02036
finding_summary.insights: Failure to generate, preserve or evaluate a reversed amide is ruled out as the explanation for the missed score target. The direct comparisons show limited measured benefit: three source pairs tie, including the leading sampled amide pair, and the only incumbent gain combines two edits. The largest task-level loss occurred in docking, where 20 reversal-bearing candidates entered pools but none was selected. That loss cannot be read as an observed penalty on a scored reversed amide; opening an empty-menu action changes later random draws, pool composition and search history even when the new alternative is unselected. A contribution probe that distinguishes the local alternative's value from these trajectory changes remains informative. The change also does not establish globally better chemistry. Eligible-amide-containing emissions increased from 328 to 563, yet measured nonaromatic C(=O)-N coverage stayed nearly flat at 1,669 versus 1,667 molecules, and mean heavy-atom count increased from 33.39 to 35.43. The molecular assessment associates the weak docking seed with a less aliphatic-amine-rich branch and still finds reactive linkages, oversized repeated cores and unspecified stereochemistry. These are descriptive associations, not causal functional-group effects. The evidence supports a narrowly correct local transformation with sparse direct score exposure; broader utility and practical chemical quality remain open.

Population standard deviation across seed means fell from 0.013310 to 0.007408. Every seed's macro score declined; the 15 paired task outcomes comprised three wins, eight losses and four ties. The molecular assessment associates the weak docking seed with a less aliphatic-amine-rich branch and still finds reactive linkages, oversized repeated cores and unspecified stereochemistry. These are descriptive associations, not causal functional-group effects. The evidence supports a narrowly correct local transformation with sparse direct score exposure; broader utility and practical chemical quality remain open.

The evidence supports a narrowly correct local transformation with sparse direct score exposure; broader utility and practical chemical quality remain open.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles retain useful amides and amines, but reactive bonds, oversized repeats and unspecified stereochemistry persist.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Read the complete Child and Parent panels for seeds 0, 1 and 2 on every supplied task. Each Child task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The output is dominated by substituted aromatic and heteroaromatic ring systems, with secondary amides, cyclic carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles, ethers, amines and halogens. Saturated and bridged nitrogen rings are well represented in some streams; ring chemistry is not missing. Digest ring-closure presence rates range from 0.9747 to 0.9931, and aromatic-atom presence rates from 0.9414 to 0.9885. These are SMILES-text presence rates, not ring counts or fractions of atoms that are aromatic. There is moderate structural variety across seeds, but each seed repeatedly revisits its own ring family. Plausibility is mixed: conventional secondary amides and aminomethyl heterocycles coexist with N-halogen bonds, O-halogen bonds, peroxides, unusual ring fusions and very large repeated heterocycles. All task digests have stereocentre_rate 0.0: no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry is recorded, although several saturated ring structures contain potential stereocentres. Almost entirely uncharged strings do not establish absence of protonatable amines. Size and functional-group descriptions below are structural readings of the supplied SMILES; reported objective values are existing trajectory values. The chemical observations do not establish synthesis routes, binding poses or activation of the registered mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly moderate-sized substituted fused heterocycles: mean SMILES length 46.5, with ring and aromatic presence both 0.9839 and halogen presence 0.9713. The leading seed-1 molecules are indoles connected by a secondary carboxamide to fluoropyridine, carrying methoxy, ethyl, vinyl and additional aryl halogen substituents. The leading cited molecule contains 26 heavy atoms. Both amide orientations occur. Seed 0 instead develops more extensively fused, N-methylated rings with imine or oxime linkers; seed 2 includes rearranged sulfur-containing fused rings and N-N-containing acyl linkers. These alternatives are much less conventional than the straightforward indole amides. The end of seed 2 still includes a peroxide-bearing, N-fluorinated amidine analogue and a small carbamoyl fluoride fragment.
liabilities: Near-leading molecules contain N-Br or N-F bonds, including a benzene-fused four-membered nitrogen ring. Chemical parseability does not establish its stability or synthetic accessibility.
Other cited proposals contain peroxide, hydrazine-like N-N or imine functionality, and terminal proposals can collapse to small reactive fragments instead of preserving the ring system.
missing_features: Retention of a complete heteroaromatic partner and intact secondary amide is inconsistent across proposals, although the leading seed shows both and the fragmented tail lacks them.

Chemically conservative variation around the leading ring/amide relationship is limited compared with ring contraction and N-halogenation. An absent target-specific scaffold or a required amide direction cannot be inferred from these scores.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It keeps a small population of high-scoring parents, while an archive of all accepted observations trains a fingerprint Gaussian process. Correlated draws from that model select which fresh offspring receive evaluations. The Parent also checks that each pool molecule has a stable canonical identity, so uniqueness and later feedback use consistent keys. Its edits readily change individual atoms, but offer no direct way to reverse an intact amide between two attached fragments.
approach.novelty: Add a direct orientation reversal of an acyclic secondary amide. Keep both attached fragments and the complete amide group, and exchange which fragment connects through nitrogen and which through the carbonyl carbon. The move becomes available when the existing atom-replacement draw lands on an eligible carbonyl carbon whose ordinary replacement menu is empty. Earlier siblings protected carbonyl endpoints, retained ring cores, or relocated nitrogen within an aromatic ring. This experiment changes the direction of a complete amide relationship, giving the existing learned selector a new local alternative without growing or trimming the molecule.

research_intent.mechanism: Enable a direct formula-preserving reversal of an acyclic secondary amide at an otherwise empty carbonyl-carbon replacement site, exchanging the nitrogen-side and carbonyl-side attachment relationships while retaining both external fragments.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: The Parent completes every supplied task and has three-seed macro mean 0.5443738005952443 with population SD 0.013310111166991866, but only 565 of 4,350 evaluated offspring beat their best generating parent. Its stable-identity addition preserves every evaluated molecule and score. The narrower graph-production limitation addressed here is that it cannot directly vary the orientation of an intact secondary amide while keeping its attached fragments: at a carbonyl carbon the inherited replacement menu is empty because bond valence is four and carbon is the only permitted element, whereas replacing a neighboring amide nitrogen can destroy the functional group. A read-only eligibility audit of the Parent's supplied trajectories, using the exact local rule below, finds 343 eligible sites in 328 of 4,350 evaluated offspring and one site in each of four unique initial molecules, giving 60 eligible initial occurrences across the supplied sessions. These counts establish available source chemistry, not that every site was drawn or that its reversed analogue would score better. The carbonyl-protection sibling preserved C=O yet 93 evaluated descendants changed an original carbonyl's neighboring atom class, including 41 losing adjacent nitrogen, and macro score fell by 0.034753. The ring-core sibling also lost macro score despite preserving rings. Conversely, the aromatic-nitrogen relocation sibling exposed 30 evaluated positional edits and one immediate new task best, showing that a coordinated local alternative can reach this selector without establishing that a different isomerization will help.
research_intent.revisit_rationale: The Knowledge-only carbonyl-protection result settles that excluding existing C=O endpoints from replacement can preserve that pair without preserving adjacent functional-group roles or improving this method's scores. It does not test a direct complete-amide orientation alternative. Revisit that functional-group question with a materially different action: open an otherwise empty carbonyl-carbon site to a paired C/N exchange and relocation of its existing oxygen, retaining the entire secondary amide, formula and both attached fragments. No native replacement choice is forbidden, and no carbonyl-protection rule is reinstated. The current Parent also retains stable pool-identity admission, while the completed aromatic-nitrogen sibling supplies evidence that the learned selector can expose coordinated local isomers. These are changed mechanism and applicability conditions, not evidence that amide reversal has already succeeded; the new orientation mechanism should retain its own stable definition rather than rewrite the earlier exclusion cluster.
